axis: a surface that merely shades the truth → a covering got up to misrepresent it

members.tone: British spelling of the same deceptive surface: a creditable tint lent to something so it passes, and no more than a tint, where *disguise* covers.
The barest word in the set, naming only the outward or token form and leaving the misleading to be inferred, where *pretence* puts the artifice on show.
A respectable-looking surface lent to something so it seems defensible; it does not hide the thing underneath, it only shades it.
Carries the idea of a polish worked onto the outside, so the deceit is one of finish rather than of concealment as in *disguise*.
The most covering word here, not a shading of the truth but an outward form that actively misrepresents what lies under it.
British spelling, and it foregrounds the artfulness, naming the semblance as something got up rather than something merely appearing.
The same artful or simulated semblance as *pretence*, but framed as a form put on and worn, so the deceit sits in the assuming of it.
